chapters.title: Chapter 426 disgusting little thing...
paragraphs: Tens of thousands of kilometers from Valemont, there was a small, remote forest. It lay deep within the Rose Empire, a flat region rich in agriculture.
In this forest, there was a little girl dressed in a commoner's dress. She had a big smiling face and bright eyes as she collected herbs.
Being a border region, the place had considerable military activity. Hordes of beasts invaded from the west, and evil necromancers hid far from the heart of power of the vast Rose Empire.
Still, she walked around that place in a very relaxed manner.
Her bare feet sank into the soft grass as she crouched down, picking up another herb and placing it in her basket.
She bent her scraped knees, ready to get up and go to the next herb.
But suddenly, she stopped.
The air felt heavy and stuffy, the pleasant breeze from before completely gone.
She tried to breathe, but no air entered her lungs. Her little legs trembled and she fell on her bottom.
"Ah... ah..." She tried to speak, but no air came with her voice, only muffled crackles escaping from her throat.
Slowly and painfully, she turned her face.
The older children used to tell her stories. Stories of monsters of darkness, who hunted in the woods and ate children.
She never believed them.
Even if she did, she was a brave child.
She always puffed out her chest, boasting about how she would defeat any monster with a single blow.
But there, she saw it.
The oldest and deepest terror. A pair of red eyes stared at her. It was an ancient terror, a distorted figure with exposed bones and guts hanging from its open belly.
Its face, like that of an old man over a hundred years old, had the left half taken over by maggots. The right side displayed blackened skin, stuck to the bone.
It was a demon; no, an evil spirit that fed on souls and fear.
Endless tears streamed down the little girl's face. She struggled to close her eyes, trying not to see that thing approaching.
Unfortunately, she no longer had control of her own body.
The world seemed to have stopped spinning. Everything around her, except for that thing, had suddenly frozen.
And then, when the creature was just one step away from the child, it was the creature that froze. Just as the little girl had frozen.
Its body lost strength, and when it realized it, a sea of shadows surrounded it.
"What a disgusting little thing..." A voice echoed, masculine and noble, carrying a soft, angry growl.
At the same moment, a hand emerged from the sea of shadows, grabbing the creature's skull and crushing it. A sea of flames engulfed the creature.
It could see only one thing: a pair of cruel, deep purple eyes staring at it as if it were just another insect, not an ancient terror.

"It's okay, sweetie, don't look..." A female voice came from behind the little girl, covering her eyes and pulling her into a protective embrace. Ruxue took out a mental calm pill, one of the few in the temple that could be given to a mortal without causing them to explode. With a gentle movement, she placed it in the little girl's mouth,
making her swallow it and hugging her a little tighter.
Qingyi just watched that scene before shaking his head gently, looking around.
He could feel those figures watching from the shadows.
Dozens, hundreds. Creatures of distorted shapes, their bodies taken over by rot. Guts spilled onto the ground and bones were exposed as they walked toward him.
He felt no fear, only displaying a small, gentle smile, calling forth the flames of primordial chaos.
"You want to see terror? Very well... I'll show you true fear. Qingyi growled. His body was engulfed by a sea of gray flames that soon
spread.
Like a tsunami of flames, they engulfed those spirits, who, for the first time in millennia, felt pain.
Not emulated pain, not fake pain. Real pain.
Their own souls burned. The very foundation of what formed them and placed them on this earth to reap the lives of poor mortals
unlucky enough to fall into their trap.
Their cries of pain and despair were in no way quieter than those of the mortals whose lives they had taken.
When the gray flames ceased and the air began to flow again, Qingyi focused only on Ruxue and the little girl in her arms.
Little by little, the child gained courage, her mind calming as the pill she received from Ruxue began to take effect.
She looked at the strange woman who was hugging her. Beautiful,
with deep purple eyes and a mature, arrogant face, yet strangely
welcoming.
And then she looked at the man approaching. He was also handsome, with protective features and a gentle smile.
Both wore strange clothes and seemed to wield strange powers.
"Tell me your name, little one." Qingyi knelt in front of her, stroking
her golden hair.
"A-Alice..." she finally managed to say, her voice still trembling and her
eyes still teary.
Her eyes flowed over Qingyi, until they finally reached his chest. More specifically, the pendant he wore, its gold contrasting with his
elegant black robes.
"A-are you a hero? My aunt said that only heroes wore these necklaces..." She asked, gaining a little more courage and pointing
towards Qingyi's pendant.
"Uh? Have you seen someone with a necklace like this before?" Qingyi
asked, his eyes shining softly.
"Hm-hmmm..." Alice nodded with a nasal sound. "It's the scary aunt... she's staying at the church for a few days..."
"Oh... can you take us to her? Don't worry, I'll protect you."
Alice hesitated for a brief moment, but in the end, she just nodded, gathering courage in her chest.
She was the bravest among her siblings. She couldn't stay behind
there.
Raising her little index finger, she just pointed in the direction and guided Qingyi through the forest to the church where she lived, a few miles from the city, which also served as an orphanage.
It was a white concrete and stone building, not very unique in architecture for that region.

Qingyi approached the church with Ruxue. He passed through the central gate and then stopped, suddenly turning his face to the right. Then he saw her: a pair of eyes as green as a lush forest on a sunny
day, focused on his.
The owner of these eyes had long, blonde hair, adorned with a tiara of
vines and flowers; a pair of pointed ears peeking out from between the golden strands that framed her noble, sharp face. Qingyi's eyes remained focused on hers for a brief moment before
they dropped, passing through her body; tall and slender, no more than a few centimetres shorter than Qingyi.

Her firm breasts were protected by a steel plate and below that, she wore a single piece of tight dark clothing that clung perfectly to her body, sinking into the curve of her slim belly and extending over the
full, perfect orbs of her ass.
Qingyi swallowed hard as his eyes traveled down her hips, reaching her shapely thighs and long legs, before rising again. Everything about her was perfect, so thin that the bones of her
delicate ribs and wide hips were faintly visible under the fabric of her clothes, her abdomen displaying soft muscles.
Yet she had fat in all the right places and only there; her breasts, her
thighs, her ass...
How could such a woman exist and be found so casually, walking among mortals?
The woman's hands reached for the beautiful sword she carried at
her waist, slender and delicate, the most perfect elven craftsmanship, its silver blade adorned with runes.
Her was face cold and impassive as her full, rosy lips parted.

Its trunk left the ground, exhaling a putrid mist from which beings like those he had killed before emerged.
Dozens, hundreds, thousands...
The number just kept growing without stopping, and soon, the entire surrounding forest had been taken over.
Aeryn shuddered slightly, but did not retreat. Finally, Qingyi could feel her mana at full strength, spreading without limits, clinging to every tree, every branch.
With a single movement of her fingers, thousands of thorns appeared, destroying everything around them, reaching the bodies of those ancient terrors and tearing them apart.
In a single moment, more than half of them turned to dust.
Panic seemed to take hold of the tree as its enormous roots pressed against the ground, trying to escape.
Obviously, Aeryn didn't allow it.
With a smooth movement, she lunged forward, her body turning into
a blur, her blade sinking into the wood and cutting the tree in two.

"Damn... Damn... damn... why the hell did this damn woman come after
me? I need a new... a new body, fast!"

"Hm... bad idea..." The handsome young man murmured softly, his lips curving into a gentle smile.
And at that moment, the spirit saw a figure emerging from behind
Qingyi.
It was enormous, as big as a castle-no, even bigger.

Its jaws bore endless rows of sharp teeth, and its beautiful purple eyes, identical to Qingyi's, watched the spirit with contempt. Qingyi barely paid attention to it for more than a moment before planting his left leg and spinning his right, striking the tree trunk. A sea of gray flames immediately spread, an ancient cry of pain and despair filling the forest as the flames of Primordial Chaos consumed
everything.
Qingyi didn't keep them active for long, his right arm burning painfully as he extinguished them.
They were still difficult to control; as he grew stronger, the flames
also grew stronger and, naturally, much more violent.
Aeryn's eyes focused on those flames for another brief moment before she turned away.
"It is profane," she said, before rising into the skies. This time, she flew
a little higher than before.

The closed forest around them opened up into a small clearing.

"We preserve balance, not nature.

balance too?" She turned her beautiful face slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 430 He cannot be a chosen hero!
paragraphs: The capital of the Rose Empire was enormous, with a population of fifty million.
Its walls, which stretched for hundreds of kilometers, were over a hundred meters high, made of white concrete and adorned with dazzling golden towers.
Yet despite the colossal height of this wall, three large buildings could be seen above it.
The first was a foreign architecture called the Pavilion of the Five colours, a strange structure, but respected by the locals.
The salaries were good, and the meals served in the restaurant on the lower floor were unique but pleasant.
The second was the capital's cathedral, a huge building of marble and gold, with towers that pierced the skies and powerful mana
formations surrounding it.
It was the second greatest source of power for the Church of Auranys on the entire continent.
Its power and beauty were second only to the cathedral in the Divine Kingdom of Auranys, home of the Divine Queen and spiritual leader of the entire religion.
And last, of course, was the Imperial Palace.
It was a building over five hundred thousand years old. A fortress that had seen the fall of countless generations, the rise of great emperors, and the ruin of tyrants, but still stood.
There were also the many magical towers surrounding the capital, but these were not exactly within the walls, existing on high flying islands above the city.
At that very moment, things in the huge cathedral of Auranys were turbulent.
Inside, the bishop of that cathedral was kneeling before a golden statue bearing the gentle smile of a woman.
Outwardly, he looked like a young man, no more than thirty years old. In reality, he was already approaching sixty thousand years of age.
The bishop was in the Eleventh Ring, equivalent to the Ancestral Emperor's Kingdom, a single step away from reaching the Twelfth Ring and he had seen many things.

From when, in retaliation for their attempted invasion, the draconic elves unleashed Khaedryss, slayer of immortals and butcher of empires upon them, killing more than half a billion and five emperors, one after another, to the recent rise of demonic forces.
Yet, despite all he had lived through and seen, there had never been a moment when his goddess was completely silent. Not until now.
The bishop knelt down, his eyes gently closing as he called out to his goddess, again and again.
But there was no response.

For some reason, strangely after Lucien, one of the candidates to be one of the five heroes, arrived on the eastern continent and had his position confirmed after a duel, she completely stopped responding. The bishop doubted very much that this had any direct connection, but still, it was something that continued to bother him.
With a sigh, he simply stood up upon hearing rapid footsteps approaching on the horizon.
From the large golden doors, a figure emerged, his blond hair bathed in the light that streamed through the many lancet windows that decorated that place.
That was Lucien. Although not yet the strongest of heroes, his presence was powerful and very important to the people of the
capital.
"Your Holiness, I heard that Aeryn was coming back, is that true?"
Lucien asked, his eyes shining.
He was honestly happy.
He had never been very interested in women after what happened with Margareth, not until he saw the three heroines who would soon join him on his adventure to purge evil.
His heart almost burst out of his chest, and suddenly all that talk of sin was gone.
He may have had his Margareth taken from him, but that mattered little now.
Margareth was beautiful, of course, but compared to Aeryn? It was simply unfair to put them side by side.

To further excite Lucien, the delay in finding the last hero was making the Divine Queen anxious. She seemed to be on the verge of ordering them to just go ahead with their prophesied mission already.
Just him alone with three beautiful heroines...
That thought immediately made Lucien salivate.
"Yes," the bishop nodded, watching Lucien's facial expression with a hint of disappointment.
Whatever was going through that young man's mind, he didn't like it.
He still remembered when Lucien was too pure to even think about touching a woman.
Well, he still was, but now more out of cowardice than purity.
In the end, the bishop could only sigh in defeat.
Lucien was a man of the Goddess; he would soon understand that he
should be above carnal desires and should preserve his chastity
without having to wear a chastity belt to do so.
'Not that any of those women are interested in him... The bishop thought, remembering when Lucien once tried to hug Aeryn.
It wasn't a pretty sight, and the cathedral's healers needed a long time
to fix all of Lucien's teeth.
"Come on, Aeryn should be here by now," the bishop said.

He walked through the long, luxurious corridors of the cathedral, greeted by powerful paladins, until he finally reached the courtyard. The courtyard overlooked the long central street, the black iron wall, and the garden that surrounded it.
Looking ahead, he saw a commotion begin. The gates opened, and then a figure appeared.
She was beautiful, more beautiful than anything the men there had
ever seen.
Her elegant blonde hair danced in the gentle breeze, a faint drop of sweat trickling down her delicate chin and landing on her steel
breastplate.
Lucien's eyes sparkled and he took a step forward.
'Aeryn-sama!' he shouted in his mind and almost in reality.
But in the next moment, he realized.
Behind her was a second figure, a man Lucien knew well.
The young man from another continent, with a face of incomparable
beauty, always wearing a gentle smile and wrapped in pure white
robes.
Although he looked different, with purple eyes and black robes,
Lucien needed only a single moment to know.
That was Long Qingyi.
Lucien's eyes focused on the bishop, and he drew his sword, noticing
the pendant on Qingyi's chest.
"Your Holiness! This cannot be real! He cannot be a chosen hero! He is
a sinner! I heard the voice of Auranys, the Goddess asked me to exterminate him personally!"
Lucien roared, his face full of rage.

chapters.title: Chapter 431 One ball
paragraphs: "Young Master Lucien, it's been a long time... I see you still haven't gotten over the outcome of our honorable duel," Qingyi replied. Despite the respectful tone in his voice, his lips curled in contempt. "Honorable duel? You used disgusting tactics to defeat me, and you still claim that it was honorable? Do you know how much I suffered to recover from that?"
"Uh? Come on..." Qingyi laughed, his purple eyes filled with a soft glow as strands of draconic Qi flooded his eyeballs. "It couldn't have been that bad, right?"
The moment his eyes focused between Lucien's legs, watching the mana flow through his body, he realized it and then fell silent.
He could see the strands of mana running through Lucien's entire body, from his skin to his bones, but there was something strange. Something was missing.
'Why is there only one?' Qingyi wondered, and soon the realization
came.
Lucien now had only one ball.
Noticing Qingyi's strange gaze and smile, Lucien immediately crossed his legs.
"You bastard, you know what you've done!" Lucien roared, looking at the Bishop. "Your Holiness, allow me to get rid of him! I am ready to defeat him now! He does not deserve the light of Auranys!"
The Bishop heard the words but did not respond immediately. Aeryn, who was watching everything with a confused look, soon realized something, her face filling with subtle amusement.
"Oh... that was unnecessarily cruel," she whispered softly.
"Exactly!" Lucien roared again.
"See, Your Holiness? Lady Aeryn agrees with me! Allow me to fight him."
"That was a compliment," Aeryn said.
For the first time in the many months Lucien had known the elven princess, she let a laugh escape her lips.
It was short, low, and soft, but enough to completely melt Lucien's heart.
Ignoring him completely, Aeryn simply sat down on a bench.
Her beautiful green eyes focused on Qingyi, her left hand rising to her hair to brush away a strand of golden hair that covered her long, pointed ears.
Her pale, slightly sweaty skin seemed to glow in the morning sun as her slender, shapely legs crossed.
She looked at the Bishop.
"My mission is complete, and I have already brought Qingyi here. I believe I am free to go, correct?" she asked.
"Yes, Your Highness," the Bishop finally replied, a tired sigh escaping his lips as his eyes focused on Qingyi again.

"You must be Long Qingyi. I received a rather interesting letter from the Bishop of the Kingdom of Valemont, and an even more interesting one from a local nun. Tell me, what do you have against Lucien?"
"Nothing," Qingyi shook his head, surprised that this man already knew of his existence.
Well, he wasn't exactly laying low, and a man like that would naturally have a wide intelligence network.
"We exchanged a few blows some time ago, but nothing more than that."
"Hm..." The Bishop scratched his chin.

"The prophecy said that regardless of who it was, if they were the one who rescued and was accepted by the Golden Convergence Pendant, they would be worthy of becoming one of the five heroes who would purge the evil of this generation and receive the blessing of Auranys... Tell me, is this what you desire?"
"Yes," Qingyi replied short and to the point.
The Bishop just looked at Lucien again.
"You may fight Qingyi. Once, in a single combat. After that, you must erase all bitterness from your heart and follow nothing but Auranys."
Lucien gritted his teeth at those words, gripping the hilt of his sword even tighter. He took a step forward and then, finally, released his golden holy power.
During this time, he had trained like a madman, using the blessing he had received from Auranys to form one ring after another. Now, he
was on the ninth ring.
His power had increased so much because of that blessing; how could
Qingyi compare?
"No tricks, no magic, just brute force," Lucien said, throwing his
sword to the ground.
He wanted to beat Qingyi with his bare hands, wanted to crush him like an insect.
Fortunately, of all the improvements he had made, his body was the most significant, undergoing the most grueling tempering that a mana-using warrior could endure.
If he could shape steel with his bare hands, why couldn't he break Qingyi's spine?
The handsome young man just stared at Lucien for a moment, his eyes turning to Aeryn, or more specifically, to the figure that
appeared beside her.
The elven beauty trembled softly, a pair of delicate hands falling on her shoulders, two huge, soft twin mounds pressing against the high
elf's delicate back.
A beautiful, delicate face appeared above Aeryn's shoulders, blue hair cascading down, joining the elf's golden hair.

Behind this figure, her body continued to emerge from a spatial fold, covered in an elegant blue dress. The fabric ran from her neckline to her waist, no less slender than Aeryn's, and then down to her protruding hips and thick, soft thighs.

Her fair, creamy skin was revealed by vertical slits in her dress, white stockings rising to the middle of her thighs, squeezing the soft flesh and forcing it to spill out into a plump, pillowy mound.
"So, elf sister... which one do you think will win?" she asked, adjusting
her hat on her head, her red lips parting in a wide smile.
"I'm not your sister, Sapphire," Aeryn replied, blushing softly and
eliciting a laugh from the blue-haired beauty.
"Oh... so cold and cruel..." Sapphire murmured in response to Aeryn,
her red lips curving into a soft smile.
She sat down next to the elf, watching the exchange with interest.
Qingyi watched the two for a brief moment.
Margareth had told him about the three heroines. Aeryn was one of them, a light and quick swordswoman, while Lucien was a powerful
tank.
That woman, Sapphire, had just used a space spell and, naturally, could only be the mage of that group.
One of the most prestigious magicians of the young generation on the continent and the heir to the Blue Tower, one of the three great
towers of magicians.
Qingyi's purple, beautiful, and piercing eyes met Sapphire, her eyes
no different from a beautiful, polished jewel.

such a pendant would never fall into the hands of someone like that
Orc Warlord.

An elf and a voluptuous, perfect mage.
How could he, the future Dragon God of Corruption, deny that?
His name would be disgraced for ten generations if he dishonored his lineage like that.

chapters.title: Chapter 433 The Emperor
paragraphs: "What are your reasons, Long Qingyi? I don't believe you want to convert to Auranys, right?" The bishop asked as he walked side by side with Qingyi.
Right behind them, Aeryn and Sapphire followed silently.
"What do you mean by that?" Qingyi turned his face. This time, the answer came in the form of a sound transmission.

[Lucien is part of the church, as is the other sister, so they naturally have every reason to be heroes. Aeryn is an elven princess and is here more for political reasons, gathering information, and duty. The same goes for Sapphire.
You, on the other hand, is just a young man of transcendental talent, a foreigner who does not have the gift of light and therefore no reason to embark on this journey.]
'Hm... Qingyi scratched his chin.
Honestly, he himself didn't have an exact reason.
He just couldn't stay in the Kingdom of Valemont, not for much longer.
He needed a place where he could grow, where he could find challenges and push his limits.
In this world, there were only the Rose Empire and the Illuminated Sky Empire where he could continue to grow, at least ignoring places like the Land of Elves and the Land of Beasts.

'What can I say? That I'm interested in stealing heroines, fucking those fat, virgin pussies, and one day, having my cock between his goddess's tits??' Qingyi thought, quickly pushing this thought out of his head.
He was brave, but not stupid.
"It's not a noble reason." Qingyi finally replied, raising a hand and calling upon his spiritual root of light, his body being surrounded by gold. "I just want to break through my limits."
The bishop stopped in his tracks, feeling the light surrounding Qingyi.
It was neither mana nor divine power, but it was so clear, so pure... How could something like this exist? Was that a reaction from the pendant?
"No.." The bishop shook his head. It came from Qingyi himself.
He swallowed hard and then continued walking. "Is that what the people of the east call a spiritual root?"
"Yes," Qingyi nodded, eliciting a sigh from the bishop.
In his tens of thousands of years of life, he had fought against cultivators only a handful of times, killing only two whose level was equivalent to his.
He really still had a lot to learn about these warriors.
They continued walking for a moment before the bishop suddenly halted his steps.
They had arrived at a large chamber many tens of meters below the cathedral.
Its interior, though darkened, was adorned with white marble, gold, and rare jewels.
But none of that caught anyone's attention there, nothing compared to the man who was kneeling in front of one of the many statues, praying silently.
He was a tall man, and even from behind, Qingyi could see the power of his body.
His shoulders were broad, his black cloak unable to hide his powerful muscles.
His aura was so subtle, so silent, similar to Aeryn's in a way, but
different.
Her aura was like a gentle breeze; that figure's was like a caged beast forced to remain silent.
"Your Majesty!" The bishop immediately fell to his knees, and even Aeryn and Sapphire followed suit, with Qingyi being the last to kneel.
That man was the Emperor of the Rose Empire, a being who had reigned for countless generations and was among the five most powerful in all of Immortal Heaven.
Qingyi had heard countless rumors about him, especially about his contacts with the Emperor of the Illuminated Heaven Empire.
Many said that they only did not kill each other because if they did not break their stalemate, the Immortal Heaven itself would break.
Of course, these were just rumors, but Qingyi already knew well that cultivators of the Ancestral Body Realm had enough power to make an entire continent tremble.
He had felt this firsthand once.
"Are you aware that the Sword Saint has returned from the Immortal Graveyard? His clash with the Sword Saint of that distant land ended in a draw, again." The Emperor turned around.
His face was covered by a steel mask, a single, huge darkened scar tearing from his chin to his neck.
With a gentle movement, he signaled for them to stand up.
"Yes, my Emperor. He came to visit me. The news from the west is
troubling."
"It is... Does the goddess insist that her heroes deal with this?" The Emperor asked, stopping a single step away from Qingyi, his eyes sweeping over him coldly with a subtle hint of hostility.
They were blue, similar to Sapphire's, but with cruelty instead of her usual playfulness.
Qingyi was already a tall man, and with his improved lineage, he had grown a few more inches, reaching one meter ninety. But even so, he was still a head shorter than the Emperor.

"They are the heroes of this generation, those chosen by fate... The goddess would never send them if she were not certain of their victory." The bishop declared, eliciting a long, cold grunt from the
Emperor.
"I just want to fix the problem quickly. The risk is increasing more and
more, and soon we will have to intervene personally. When that happens, there will be blood.
You will be on the front line, so you should worry about this more than anyone else." The Emperor whispered, more like a threat than
anything else.
The bishop shuddered, but in the end, he could only sigh.
'Goddess... Where are you to guide me out of this situation?' He asked
himself.
Soon, he would have to make a trip to the Divine Kingdom. Ignoring him, the Emperor just kept walking, stopping in front of Sapphire, who had already separated from Aeryn.
"Father..." Sapphire lowered her head. She had never been given permission to call this man that, but she did so anyway.
The Emperor remained impassive.
He moved his hand slightly toward Sapphire's face, but in the end, he simply left, his body disappearing into thin air.

chapters.title: Chapter 434 Most urgent matter
paragraphs: After the emperor left, Qingyi had to endure a seemingly endless series of rituals.
Finally, they confirmed what was necessary: the pendant had accepted him.
In reality, Qingyi had been rejected in almost all of these rituals.
However, all it took was a slight trace of his bloodline Qi to suddenly solve the entire problem.
Apparently, even magical arrays recognized that, sometimes, it was better to give in so as not to be shattered.
After all this, Qingyi had a long conversation with the bishop.
There, he learned more about the current political situation of the Rose Empire and his true mission.
Of course, the bishop did not say too much.
All Qingyi knew was that, in some way, it had something to do with the ancestral spirit that he and Aeryn had eliminated in that forest.
After all that, Qingyi was released.
He even received his own residence in the capital, decided by the church itself.
Their goddess must have been fuming to see her followers treating so well someone she hated so much.
But honestly, it wasn't exactly a luxurious place.
Still, it was certainly more than enough for an imperial middle-class family to live in.
It was a two-story concrete and wood building.
The house had two bathrooms and two bedrooms, as well as a kitchen
and a nicely furnished living room.
It was one of many houses that the church kept ready for mid-level officials and priests.
After making sure everything was in order and checking that there were no magical spying devices, Qingyi left.
But now, he was accompanied.
At his right side was Jin Meilin, whose noble face and beautiful black eyes showed deep impression.
She really couldn't believe that one day in her life she would be able to see a city whose glory, size, and beauty were equivalent to that of the Illuminated Imperial Capital.
Margareth, on the other hand, had lived in the capital for a long time.
Right now, she kept her eyes focused on one of the many magical towers surrounding the city.
When she left this region, she had barely reached the fifth ring.
Although talented, she was simply not comparable to the true great geniuses.
She was very lucky to have even been selected by the church to manage those lands in the east.
But now, everything had changed.
She had recently reached the ninth ring, just before Isabel Valemont reached the seventh ring.
But that wasn't all.
Although Feiyan couldn't make pills for her, Qingyi still bought enough pills for her to raise her mana heart to the transcendent level.
She was no longer just an above-average talent.
Qingyi noticed her gaze and brought his hands to her long golden hair, caressing it.
"If you want, we can go there soon. I haven't been given any
responsibilities yet," Qingyi said.
"But first, we have to go to the Five Colors Pavilion. Your husband needs to cultivate a little, hahaha."
Qingyi laughed loudly, planting a kiss on Margareth's cheek.
Ignoring the envious glances, he simply walked toward the huge building on the horizon.
The Five Colors Pavilion branch in the Rose Empire was simply incomparable to the branch in the Blue Sea Kingdom.
It was easily twice the size and was guarded by an Ancestral Emperor.
The moment Qingyi, Margareth, and Meilin entered there, the air
around them changed.
From the darkness that took over the floor, a figure emerged.
That was one of the Shadows of the Gold King.
"Young Miss Meilin, it is an honor to have you here."
The shadow bowed, turning its face toward Qingyi.
'So that was the man Young Miss Meilin had chosen, a True Immortal despite being only in his early twenties. That wasn't bad at all.'
"Young Master Qingyi." The shadow bowed again.
"I want to talk to my father, are the communication arrays working?" Meilin asked, stepping forward.
"Certainly, young lady."
The shadow spoke and quickly guided them to the upper floors and
then to his office.
There wasn't even a hint of displeasure on his face as he gave up his chair to Jin Meilin.
At the end of the day, he was a servant of the Gold King, but also a
servant of the Gold King's children.
Unless it was directly against an order from the Gold King himself, the
word of his children was law.
Of course, this didn't apply to everyone.
In the end, only those whom the shadows saw value in could be
treated so well.
The shadows' only obligation to the rest was to keep them alive and breathing, nothing more.
While Meilin and Margareth made contact with the other continent,
the shadow guided Qingyi to one of the many cultivation rooms in
that huge building.
There, the handsome young man locked himself in.
Honestly, the Qi density wasn't good.
This was probably due to the lack of spirit veins and the fact that this
cultivation room was only maintained by superior Qi crystals.
But Qingyi didn't think much of it.
It was, at least, infinitely superior to cultivating in an environment
where the Qi around him was depleted with every breath he took.
With a soft sigh, Qingyi knelt down, opening his status screen.
[Name: Long Qingyi
Age: 21
Cultivation: First Stage Of The True Immortal Realm (5T lust points to
upgrade)
Affinities: Lightning: 1500 - Sword: 1000 - Fire: 1500 - Ice: 1500 -
Space: 1500 Light: 1500 Shadow: 1500 - Charm: 1500 (can be
upgraded in the lust store)
Spiritual roots: Immortal-level Primordial Creation Seed spirit root
(Lightning, sword, fire, ice, space, light, shadow) (10T lust points to upgrade, new roots can be bought in the lust store).
Lineage: Blood of the Corruption Dragon God (Transcendental grade,
10T lust points to upgrade.)
Constitution: Primordial Dragon Body (Transcendental grade, 10T lust points to upgrade.)
Those numbers didn't exactly make him excited, but he could only
shake his head.
Sure, he could have a few nights of sex with his wives, which would
be more than enough to make him rich again.
But Qingyi preferred to take care of the most urgent matter for him
first.
He had acquired new spiritual roots, but he had not acquired any techniques that utilized these new roots.

After making sure everything was in order and checking that there were no magical spying devices, Qingyi left.
But now, he was accompanied.
At his right side was Jin Meilin, whose noble face and beautiful black eyes showed deep impression.
She really couldn't believe that one day in her life she would be able to see a city whose glory, size, and beauty were equivalent to that of the Illuminated Imperial Capital.
Margareth, on the other hand, had lived in the capital for a long time.
Right now, she kept her eyes focused on one of the many magical towers surrounding the city.
When she left this region, she had barely reached the fifth ring.
Although talented, she was simply not comparable to the true great geniuses.
She was very lucky to have even been selected by the church to manage those lands in the east.
But now, everything had changed.
She had recently reached the ninth ring, just before Isabel Valemont reached the seventh ring.
But that wasn't all.
Although Feiyan couldn't make pills for her, Qingyi still bought enough pills for her to raise her mana heart to the transcendent level.
She was no longer just an above-average talent.
Qingyi noticed her gaze and brought his hands to her long golden hair, caressing it.
"If you want, we can go there soon.
I haven't been given any
responsibilities yet," Qingyi said.
"But first, we have to go to the Five Colors Pavilion.
Your husband needs to cultivate a little, hahaha."
Qingyi laughed loudly, planting a kiss on Margareth's cheek.
Ignoring the envious glances, he simply walked toward the huge building on the horizon.
The Five Colors Pavilion branch in the Rose Empire was simply incomparable to the branch in the Blue Sea Kingdom.
It was easily twice the size and was guarded by an Ancestral Emperor.
The moment Qingyi, Margareth, and Meilin entered there, the air
around them changed.
From the darkness that took over the floor, a figure emerged.
That was one of the Shadows of the Gold King.
"Young Miss Meilin, it is an honor to have you here."
The shadow bowed, turning its face toward Qingyi.
'So that was the man Young Miss Meilin had chosen, a True Immortal despite being only in his early twenties.
That wasn't bad at all.'
"Young Master Qingyi." The shadow bowed again.
"I want to talk to my father, are the communication arrays working?" Meilin asked, stepping forward.
"Certainly, young lady."
The shadow spoke and quickly guided them to the upper floors and
then to his office.
There wasn't even a hint of displeasure on his face as he gave up his chair to Jin Meilin.
At the end of the day, he was a servant of the Gold King, but also a
servant of the Gold King's children.
Unless it was directly against an order from the Gold King himself, the
word of his children was law.
Of course, this didn't apply to everyone.
In the end, only those whom the shadows saw value in could be
treated so well.
The shadows' only obligation to the rest was to keep them alive and breathing, nothing more.
While Meilin and Margareth made contact with the other continent,
the shadow guided Qingyi to one of the many cultivation rooms in
that huge building.
There, the handsome young man locked himself in.
Honestly, the Qi density wasn't good.
This was probably due to the lack of spirit veins and the fact that this
cultivation room was only maintained by superior Qi crystals.
But Qingyi didn't think much of it.
It was, at least, infinitely superior to cultivating in an environment
where the Qi around him was depleted with every breath he took.
With a soft sigh, Qingyi knelt down, opening his status screen.
[Name: Long Qingyi
Age: 21
Cultivation: First Stage Of The True Immortal Realm (5T lust points to
upgrade)
Affinities: Lightning: 1500 - Sword: 1000 - Fire: 1500 - Ice: 1500 -
Space: 1500 Light: 1500 Shadow: 1500 - Charm: 1500 (can be
upgraded in the lust store)
Spiritual roots: Immortal-level Primordial Creation Seed spirit root
(Lightning, sword, fire, ice, space, light, shadow) (10T lust points to upgrade, new roots can be bought in the lust store).
Lineage: Blood of the Corruption Dragon God (Transcendental grade,
10T lust points to upgrade.)
Constitution: Primordial Dragon Body (Transcendental grade, 10T lust points to upgrade.)
Those numbers didn't exactly make him excited, but he could only
shake his head.
Sure, he could have a few nights of sex with his wives, which would
be more than enough to make him rich again.
But Qingyi preferred to take care of the most urgent matter for him
first.
He had acquired new spiritual roots, but he had not acquired any techniques that utilized these new roots.

chapters.title: Chapter 435 Ten Thousand Shadows Devouring Art.
paragraphs: Honestly, Qingyi still didn't quite know what to do with his spiritual root of light.
Well, it was useful for trying to manipulate the feelings of some priest or perhaps illuminating a dark room. In reality, even that had little practical use.
With Qingyi's current eye and Qi sense abilities, no ordinary darkness could blind him.
With a soft sigh, he just reviewed his other techniques.
It had been a long time since he had encountered an enemy that forced him to use the Eternal Wall of the Icy Lord, and honestly, he would rather just take the hit.
His body was so powerful that it was more efficient to just accept the impact directly.
His Art of the Nine Spears of Celestial Fire, despite only being at the mortal grade, had very good scalability with his level of power.
The same was true for the Storm Monarch Sword Art.
The Heaven-Shattering Divine Slash, on the other hand, couldn't even be compared.
Its offensive power was above anything Qingyi had ever seen in his life.
With that, there was still one concern on Qingyi's mind.
His enemies.
How long had it been since he had faced an enemy that made him truly bleed? Someone who made him fight for his life?
He had lost count of how many ants he had crushed, but he could
barely remember the last time he felt close to death.
Ease leads to complacency, and complacency leads to unfounded arrogance.
In the world of cultivation, that was dangerous.
Well, it wasn't his fault that his enemies were too weak.
With a sigh, Qingyi opened the system store.
He could only hope that the "heroic journey" that bishop was so concerned about would be worth it to strengthen him.
Given the emperor's concern about it, what were the chances that they were just killing some weaklings?
Qingyi filtered his searches to find only techniques for shadows and space.
He had about thirty billion for each. With that, he could definitely buy at least two immortal-grade techniques.
Although those spiritual roots did not directly increase his power, they made him much more versatile.
They gave him the ability to freely enter shadows and break through space, but it still wasn't enough.
His spatial abilities weren't fast enough to be useful in actual combat.
His shadow abilities, while not as limited, still had their flaws.
They would be good for sneak attacks, but virtually useless against an enemy in front of him.
Exhaling heavily, Qingyi continued searching.
After a moment, he finally found something that interested him.
[Name: Ten Thousand Shadows Devouring Art.
Description: Created by the First Dark Emperor, its basis is the devouring of all light and energy, redirecting them into a single
powerful attack.
Grade: Immortal
Price: Twenty billion Lust points]
[Name: Deep Void Art.

Description: A fundamental passive art, forged for the control of the void and all space. It is capable of instantly moving any item within the user's Qi range, breaking spatial locks, and teleporting the user instantly and efficiently.
Grade: Ancestral
Price: Forty billion Lust points]
Qingyi observed the two techniques for a brief moment.
The Ten Thousand Shadows Devouring Art was more of an offensive technique, but compared to the other choices, it was better than nothing.
The Deep Void Art, on the other hand, was exactly what Qingyi needed.
The ability to freely and quickly change the position of items, break through spatial barriers, and teleport at a speed far superior to
before.
After a moment of hesitation, Qingyi clicked to purchase both
techniques.
His Lust point reserves immediately dropped to just five billion.
The next moment, a flood of information invaded his mind.

Strangely, he didn't feel the usual terrible sharp pain as what seemed like the equivalent of thousands of pages describing and teaching the use of a specific technique were pushed into his brain at once.
This time, he only felt a slight tingling sensation.
'Is this because of the Draconic Mind?' Qingyi wondered, unable to
help but feel a little impressed.
He barely felt any pressure, even though he was forced to absorb so
much knowledge.
Sighing, he simply closed his eyes.
He absorbed everything carefully, ensuring that not even a drop of knowledge escaped his mind.
After a brief moment, he opened his eyes and stood up, entering his
Sea of Mind.
Opening the system store, he drew the Heaven-Defying Thunder
Sword.
He circulated his dark Qi, and his body was immediately swallowed by
a deep sea of shadows that spread for dozens of meters.
He became one with the shadows.
Qingyi then retracted his sword, prepared himself, and muttered:
"Devour and destroy..."
The moment Qingyi's voice fell, his entire Sea of Mind changed.
Like a black hole, every photon of light was immediately sucked
toward him.
The water around him was deprived of its usual warmth as Qingyi's Qi
expanded violently.
Fifty meters.
One hundred meters.
Five hundred meters.
One kilometer. The sea of shadows finally stopped growing, pulsing once before
suddenly receding.
Qingyi gritted his teeth, feeling the density of Qi around him increase
violently.
His feet left the ground as he finally pointed the Heaven-Defying Thunder Sword forward.
From its sharp tip, a projectile emerged.
Small, almost nonexistent, but frighteningly powerful, formed from
nothing but deep darkness.
The moment this projectile was fired, a shockwave spread out.
Qingyi's body was forced back a few meters by the rebound. Surrounding the projectile of darkness was a thin layer of pure white
light swirling around it.
It propelled it with even more force, opening a tear in the air that
spread for kilometers and slowly disintegrated into fragments of light.
Finally, the projectile hit the ground.
Qingyi's eyes flashed when he saw the entire horizon taken over by a
black explosion.
An orb of shadows swallowed dozens of kilometers around it.
Its power was still dozens of times inferior to the Heaven-Shattering
Divine Slash.
However, its large-scale destructive power was certainly not inferior to the Art of the Nine Spears of Celestial Fire.

chapters.title: Chapter 436 - Deep Void Art
paragraphs: A flaming spear appeared in Qingyi's hands.
Its heat dominated everything around it, causing the water beneath his feet to instantly begin boiling.
After a brief moment, he hurled it toward the horizon, keeping his gaze fixed on it as it broke the speed of sound.
In the next moment, the bright stars in his purple pupils seemed to spin, and the space in front of the spear distorted violently, swallowing it completely.
Immediately, Qingyi felt the heat surge past his face.
He raised a single hand, grabbing the spear with his open palm. A soft grunt escaped his lips as the weapon exploded in his hand.
It was simply wonderful.
With a satisfied sigh, Qingyi threw two more spears in succession.

He activated a cheap space-blocking talisman he had purchased from the system store. An invisible barrier spread out, forming around him. Shaping his spatial Qi like a sharp blade, he attacked, moving his draconic Qi through his eyes to analyze the structure.
Like every array, that talisman was formed of lines of Qi that, together, formed something similar to an ancient programming language.
If those lines were destroyed, they would usually regenerate instantly.
However, there were exceptions, small flaws that, if struck, could cause instabilities throughout the entire array.
Of course, simply hitting them with raw Qi was not enough. In high-level spatial blocking arrays, such flaws barely existed.
And that was the use of the technique Qingyi had just discovered.
He could hit them, spread his spatial Qi inside them, and force them to collapse structurally.
Qingyi aimed at one of these Qi lines, using his spatial Qi to strike it with surgical precision.
Immediately, the world around him shattered like a broken mirror, collapsing to the ground before dissolving into fragments of light.
Qingyi had only taken a second and a half.
Even so, the two spears he had thrown were already nearly two kilometers away.
Gritting his teeth, he moved his spatial Qi with full force.
His body disappeared immediately, reappearing next to the spears flying side by side.
He grabbed both of them and teleported again, appearing a few hundred meters in the air, violently redirecting them toward the ground.
As the spears hit the ground and the explosion took over everything below, Qingyi just exhaled heavily.
He descended to the ground. The flames licked the edge of his feet before quickly dissipating into the air.
His black robes, surrounded by golden patterns, fluttered gently as a subtle smile spread across his lips.
It hadn't been an incomparable improvement in combat power, but still, it was very important to him.
Especially the ability to break through spatial locks.
After all, what would happen to him if a superior cultivation expert decided to capture him and sealed off the space to prevent him from escaping?
With such a technique, Qingyi was practically immune to this kind of attack.
With a sigh, Qingyi simply continued to train for the equivalent of a few hours in the outside world, which meant months in there.
When he felt satisfied, he finally left the sea of consciousness.
Upon stepping out of the cultivation room, he was immediately greeted by the Shadow of the Gold King.
The Shadow wore a black mask and his entire body was covered in darkened, torn robes, clashing with the luxurious corridors that surrounded him.
"Young Master Qingyi."
The Shadow bowed his head subtly in a polite greeting.
Even though he was a powerful Ancestral Emperor and Qingyi was only a True Immortal, the Shadow simply did not care about the difference in cultivation.
After all, Qingyi was the husband of the respected Young Lady Jin
Meilin and an unparalleled talent.
That alone placed him above many of the more mediocre sons of the
Gold King.
"Can we talk alone for a moment?" The Shadow asked.
Qingyi thought for a brief moment before nodding. Soon, the two
men found themselves walking side by side.
"When do you plan to visit Master Jin?" The Shadow asked as they arrived at a secluded balcony overlooking the entire capital.
He immediately sat down, took a bottle of liquor from his robes, and poured himself and Qingyi a drink.

"I don't know," Qingyi shook his head, taking a sip of the strong but sweet alcohol. "A few months. Not much more than a year or two." "Hm..." Shadow scratched his chin, a soft grunt escaping from his
covered lips.
Despite wearing a mask, he was still able to drink normally, as if the liquid passed directly through the steel.
"And are you sure you understand the danger of joining the heroes of the Church of Auranys? Would you like me to escort you?
"Oh? You know about the five heroes? Do you know what we need to
do, specifically?" Qingyi asked.
Even he hadn't received the complete information and was extremely curious about what they would need to kill.
As for the escort proposal, he would refuse it, regardless of the
enemy's power.
He didn't want any babysitters following him around.
"I know it's an unholy ritual and that it involved the demons of this
land and ours as well... they seem to be preparing something big, and whatever it is, it's about to explode."
'Something involving the demons of both lands? Demons who used demonic Qi and demons who used demonic mana?" Qingyi repeated
in his mind.
A tremor spread through his body.
What on earth could bring the two such different demonic forces
together?
Qingyi was about to ask more questions when a sweet voice echoed
behind him, catching his attention.
"Husband!"
The two beauties appeared in the hallway, their beautiful faces
glowing as they embraced Qingyi.
"Why did it take you so long to leave that cultivation room, huh? Someone from the Divine Church of Auranys came here looking for you," Margareth said, snuggling into Qingyi's arms.
"What did they want?"
"I don't know... but it seemed important. They said you should come
to the cathedral immediately. It seems to have something to do with the Sacred Priestess. She's one of the five heroines too."
"Hm..." Qingyi grunted.
He was a little dissatisfied with the idea of not being able to finish his conversation with the Shadow of the Golden King.
But that dissatisfaction only lasted until Meilin's last sentence.
A priestess and the only one of the heroines he had not yet met. Suddenly, the details of what the demonic cult was planning no longer interested him that much.

chapters.title: Chapter 437 Celestia
paragraphs: [First, the bad news: There will only be a 1,500-word chapter today (instead of 2x1,000) because I had to help my dad with his car at the repair shop. Those who follow me on Discord know what happened, but anyway, it wasn't fun, hahaha.
I'm sorry.
The good news: I quit my current job, and starting next month, the chapter release rate will increase to 3-4 per day. Fuck my boss, btw.]
"Don't you want to talk more about that sacred priestess to your lovely hubby? Qingyi asked.
The moment they found themselves alone in that closed hallway, his hands immediately flowed towards Margareth's ass.
Her eyes widened slightly as a loud, wet smack echoed.
"Nghnn~~ you... what the hell are you planning, huh?" She moaned, panting softly.
Qingyi's fingers sank into the soft flesh, which rippled like a churning sea, while his other hand flowed to Meilin on his left.
"Ah~~ Does hubby's greed really have no limit?" Meilin asked, lifting her flushed face.
A soft, high-pitched squeal escaped her lips with the impact on her fat, round, perfect ass.
"I wouldn't have you by my side if I had any limits," Qingyi said, depositing a soft kiss on Meilin's lips.
His hands moved up from the two beauties' buttocks to their slim, delicate waists.
"Celestia, that's her name," Margareth finally spoke. "She is known as Auranys' most beloved daughter and rarely shows herself. Lately, even less so."
"Hm..." Qingyi scratched his chin thoughtfully.
Auranys' most beloved daughter.
The bishop had told him about Auranys' recent refusal to answer prayers, even from her highest followers.
It was a subject that, honestly, didn't interest Qingyi much.
At least, not if he ignored the fact that, strangely, she had stopped responding to prayers and requests for instruction after Lucien arrived on the eastern continent.
In a single moment, Qingyi's mind was able to work through thousands of possibilities.
Was she weakened after that blessing to Lucien? Was something like that really capable of weakening a goddess?
Qingyi knew that it was not a small thing. Lucien had even managed
to match him in cultivation speed.
Still, she was a goddess.
As Qingyi thought, he finally stopped his steps.
They were about to leave the Five-Color Pavilion.
Allowing Margareth and Meilin to return to the world of the mind, he quickened his pace.
Whatever it was, he would find his answers soon.
In the cathedral, things were not exactly peaceful.
An armored entourage of a hundred paladins, each with power equivalent to that of a True Immortal, had completely closed off the building.
They refused to open it to anyone.
"What's going on? I have a scheduled meeting with His Holiness!" A
pompous noble stepped forward, shouting in the face of the paladins' leader.
The guard was an old warrior from the Tenth Ring.

"The bishop cannot and will not see anyone at this very moment. You may reschedule your meeting," the paladin replied coldly. "Reschedule? Do you know how difficult it was to get this meeting in the first place? I'm going to="

paragraphs: A few thousand kilometers from the imperial capital, there was a small village surrounded by dense forest.
That village was located on the border between the east and west of the empire, in a place called the Kingdom of Tempest Valley.
This kingdom was led by a grumpy but fair wizard, loyal only to the emperor and, of course, to his magical research.
Overall, it was a peaceful place, although it was quite agitated on that particular day.
"I beg your pardon, sir... but our royal suite has already been rented by a young couple... I don't believe they are willing to exchange."
A trembling voice echoed through one of the few inns that had accommodations for the nobility in that village.
"And who is this couple? I demand to know! My father paid for half the construction of this damn inn!" Another voice echoed, young and angry.
It belonged to a black-haired man with no physical power, a pathetic mortal even in front of that humble attendant, who was only in the second ring.
Still, his presence there made everyone shudder.
Not because of his ugly face, and even less because of his fat, protruding belly.
It was the man beside him; a bald, tanned bastard with dark eyes and a face covered in horrible scars.
Just standing there was more than enough for his terrifying aura to crush everyone in the reception area, the huge sword on his back glinting softly.
Even the most cruel-looking men, who had lived a life of crime, kept
their voices low and their heads even lower as they ate.
"Please, young master... your own father was the one who set our code of conduct towards customers. We can't just hand over customer information like that!" The attendant spoke again, to no avail.
"I am a nobleman, and this is my land! My word is the only law or code of conduct you will follow!"
'Noble my ass... you're basically a thug with daddy's money!' The attendant almost teared up.
Obviously, he didn't have the courage to say that out loud, and could only sigh in defeat.

How could such a noble man have such a despicable son? He was lucky that damn brat was far from the main line of succession. The attendant's lips opened to say something, but before anything came out, his eyes focused on a young couple who had just arrived. The man was tall and intimidating, his face completely covered. The woman, on the other hand, was short and sweet-looking, only her full, rosy lips visible under the cloak that covered her entire body. "Hubby... don't you want to eat anything? I heard that the people of the Storm Valley Kingdom make wonderful roast meat!"
The woman's voice echoed; low, almost a whisper, but still loud enough for everyone there to hear.
It was sweet and soft, full of the purest love and affection; the kind of voice a man could only dream of hearing her moan with.
The young nobleman immediately stepped in front of them.
"These are the ones who took the royal suite, right?" The young nobleman asked, a big smile spreading across his face as he turned to his henchman, who just shook his head.
He couldn't sense any power coming from either of those two.
The attendant just nodded silently, wanting to be as far away from there as possible.
"You there." The young man pointed at the tall man, Long Qingyi.

"I am the owner of this village and everything within a hundred kilometers around it. You took something that was mine, and I want it back now. Give me the key to the royal suite, and I will even show you kindness by refunding part of the value you paid."
Qingyi heard those words and remained silent for a brief moment.

"Hm? These lands belong to the emperor... how can you own them? Even if your family rules this land, everything belongs to the emperor in the end." Celestia spoke, looking confused by the young nobleman's words.
The man behind the nobleman just flashed a gentle smile on his rough-featured face and took a step forward.
"A beauty like you shouldn't hide your face like that, you know? Men
like us deserve to have a little fun too."
He raised his rough and powerful hand, his nearly two-meter-tall
body towering even above Qingyi.
Celestia cringed, and just before that hand touched her face, Qingyi
acted.
A loud slap echoed and the warrior's hand was thrown back.
"Do that again..." Qingyi muttered, his voice almost a growl with rage. "And I promise, I'll rip your arms from your shoulders."
"You..." The warrior gritted his teeth, a powerful murderous intent penetrating his bones, every piece of him screaming in agony.
What the hell was going on?
He looked into the eyes of that young man, the only thing visible under the cloak that covered his body.
They were purple, beautiful and piercing, covered with a murderous intent capable of making even the most hardened bandit crumble.
But that warrior was no ordinary bandit.
His fear quickly turned to anger as he roared, "Who the hell do you think you are to tell me what I can and cannot do?
He was a powerful ninth-ring expert, undefeated in this region. He would not back down in front of some pretty face.
The warrior lunged forward, trying to grab Celestia, but he was barely
able to get halfway there.
His vision darkened, a horrible pain took over his jaw, and he fell backward.
He tried to scream, but immediately found himself choking on his
own blood, his mouth reduced to nothing more than a collection of bones and flesh mangled by Qingyi's fist.
"I warned you..." For a brief moment, the warrior could see Qingyi's
face.
It was beautiful, wearing a gentle, soft smile.
He stepped on the warrior's chest and grabbed his arms.
"Celestia, close your eyes." Qingyi asked, and the moment the
golden-haired beauty nodded, he pulled.
